description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Le Havre for container ships and tankers: hull structure, pre-docking UTM and scrubber piping inside the SECA.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging in Le Havre
intro: Le Havre is France's largest container port and the Seine estuary's gateway for crude, oil products and ro-ro cargo, so most gauging here is done afloat: at the Port 2000 terminals, on lay-by berths in the inner basins or at anchor in the Baie de Seine. Superintendents call us when a ship needs its tanks and hull structure measured during a call, before a docking at a yard elsewhere. Each job is staffed by a team we mobilise from India to the ship.

highlights.h: Afloat gauging on fixed call windows
highlights.p: Container calls at Port 2000 are short, so the gauging plan is built around berth time: ballast tanks and voids first, holds only where crane work allows, and anything unfinished handed on to the docking yard.

Large ships calling at Le Havre normally dock elsewhere. Gauging during the call gives the superintendent a measured steel renewal list for the yard specification before the ship leaves the Seine estuary.

Le Havre lies inside the North Sea SOx ECA, where scrubber-fitted ships keep their systems running from the Channel approaches to the berth. Wash-water and overboard lines can be gauged while cargo is worked.

port.h: The port of Le Havre and the ships that call there
p: Le Havre sits on the north bank of the Seine estuary and is the seaward end of HAROPA PORT, the combined port authority for Le Havre, Rouen and Paris. It is France's largest container port. The Port 2000 terminals, built out into the estuary in front of the older docks, receive the big container ships of the Asia–North Europe and transatlantic services, while the inner basins behind the locks handle ro-ro, conventional cargo, port craft and ships on lay-by. Car carriers, cross-Channel ro-pax ferries to England and a regular programme of cruise calls complete the dry-cargo and passenger picture.

Energy is the port's second pillar. Crude and refined products move through the oil terminals, including the deep-water crude terminal at Antifer on the coast north of the city, and the TotalEnergies refining and petrochemical platform at Gonfreville-l'Orcher stands on the estuary. That puts crude tankers, product tankers and chemical tankers in the same roads as the container ships. Upriver, Rouen's grain terminals load bulk carriers for export, and the offshore wind turbine factory on the port's industrial zone has brought installation and service vessels into the mix.

Container calls at Port 2000 are tightly windowed, so gauging during them is limited to what fits the berth time: a set of ballast tanks, a section of deck structure or targeted readings on a known problem area. Longer windows come from ships waiting for a berth or for orders in the Baie de Seine anchorage, from lay-by stays in the inner basins between charters, and from repair calls at the old port's quays. The dry docks in the old port take small and mid-sized ships only, so the large ships that call here normally dock at yards in other countries. The distinctive demand at Le Havre is therefore pre-docking gauging: readings taken during the call that let a superintendent fix the steel renewal estimate before the ship reaches the yard.

facilities.h: Where thickness gauging is done around Le Havre
p: At the Port 2000 terminals, thickness gauging at Le Havre is fitted around cargo work. Ballast tanks, voids and the engine room can be entered once the ship's permit-to-work system allows it, but holds under working cranes are off limits, so hold readings are taken only where the chief officer and the stevedores agree a safe sequence. The inner basins are better for heavier scopes: a ship on a lay-by berth, with no cargo operations, can have a full tank programme or renewal-survey gauging worked through without interruption.

Tankers are a separate case. At the oil berths and at Antifer, cargo tanks are not entered during cargo operations and battery-powered instruments on deck in hazardous zones need the terminal's and the ship's permission. Ballast tanks on a laden arrival are usually empty, which makes the anchorage in the Baie de Seine a practical place to gauge them before berthing, weather permitting. For a laden tanker the anchorage reading is often the only chance before docking, because ballast goes in as soon as discharge starts. Rouen, up the Seine, is reached by road on the same mobilisation when a bulk carrier there needs readings.
list: Port 2000 container terminals — targeted gauging of ballast tanks, hatch coamings and cross-deck structure on container ships within the berth window.
Inner basins behind the locks — lay-by stays where a full tank programme or renewal-survey gauging can run without cargo operations.
Old-port dry docks and repair quays — gauging on ferries, dredgers, port craft and other small and mid-sized ships during docking or repair afloat.
Oil terminals and the Antifer crude terminal — ballast-tank and deck gauging on crude and product tankers within the terminal's safety rules.
Baie de Seine anchorage — launch-served gauging on ships waiting for a berth or for orders, with laden tankers' empty ballast tanks a common target.
Rouen grain terminals on the Seine — hold, hatch cover and ballast-tank gauging on bulk carriers loading grain, reached by road from Le Havre.

context.h: Regulation and market context at Le Havre
p: France applies port state control under the Paris MoU, and Le Havre's place on the main Asia–North Europe and transatlantic loops brings a steady flow of foreign-flag ships through that regime. Under the Paris MoU's risk-based targeting, older ships with a poor record are inspected more often, and visible wastage, holed air pipes or corroded hatch coamings are the kind of finding that turns an inspection into a detention. Readings taken before a call tell the master and the superintendent where the structure stands before an inspector asks.

Le Havre is inside the North Sea SOx ECA, which takes in the English Channel east of 5°W, so the 0.10% sulphur limit has applied on arrival and departure since 1 January 2015, and the EU ETS (since 2024) and FuelEU Maritime (since 2025) apply to every call. Scrubber-fitted container ships and car carriers run their systems throughout the Channel, and that duty shows up as wall loss in wash-water piping. For tankers at the oil terminals the framework is the ESP regime under SOLAS chapter XI-1 regulation 2 and IACS UR Z10.1 or Z10.4. Container ships are not ESP ships: their gauging follows the hull survey requirements of UR Z7 and their society's rules, with the extent growing at each renewal survey and hatch coamings, deck longitudinals and double-bottom tanks the usual focus.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Le Havre
jobs.p: Most Le Havre jobs are scoped around a fixed call window rather than a drydock programme. The superintendent sends the class's gauging requirements or the TM plan, the berth times and any known problem areas; we size the team so the readings that matter are taken before sailing, and the rest are left for the docking yard. Container ship thickness measurement and tanker work make up most requests:
list: Pre-docking gauging of double-bottom and side ballast tanks on a container ship during a Port 2000 call, so the steel renewal estimate is ready before the ship reaches its yard.
Wall-thickness checks on scrubber wash-water and overboard piping of a car carrier while it loads, concentrating on bends, reducers and the overboard penetration.
A first set of ballast-tank readings on a crude tanker waiting for orders in the Baie de Seine, ahead of the CAP gauging planned for its next docking.
On-hire condition gauging of holds, hatch covers and coamings on a bulk carrier before it proceeds up the Seine to load grain at Rouen.
Vehicle-deck plating, ramp structure and ballast-tank gauging on a ro-ro ship laid by in the inner basins between charters, ahead of its renewal survey.

logistics: Teams fly into Paris Charles de Gaulle and continue to Le Havre by road or rail; Paris-Orly is an alternative for some connections. The ship's agent requests ISPS gate passes for the named technicians at Port 2000 or the oil terminals, and books launch boats for ships at anchor in the Baie de Seine. France is part of the Schengen area, so every technician needs a Schengen visa: we start the applications once the call or docking window is firm and ask the owner or agent for an invitation letter naming the vessel and port. Flights are then planned against the agent's latest ETA.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a container ship during a normal Port 2000 call?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. A container call is a fixed window with cranes working the holds, so we concentrate on spaces that can be entered safely during cargo work: double-bottom and side ballast tanks, voids, the engine room and deck structure clear of the crane lanes. Holds are gauged only where the terminal and the chief officer agree a safe sequence, and anything the window does not allow is passed to the docking yard.

faqs.q: Our ship docks outside France next month. Is it worth gauging at Le Havre first?
faqs.a: Often it is. Readings taken at Le Havre turn the yard specification from an allowance into a measured steel list, which shortens the time spent in dock deciding on renewals. The class surveyor at the yard decides which readings are credited to the survey, so we agree the scope with the superintendent against the surveyor's requirements before starting.

faqs.q: Is scrubber pipe inspection in Le Havre worth doing on a ship that trades in the Channel?
faqs.a: Inside the SECA a scrubber-fitted ship runs its system continuously to meet the 0.10% sulphur equivalent, so wash-water lines, bends downstream of the pumps and the overboard penetration carry acidic flow on every passage. We gauge those lines at fixed grid points, compare against earlier readings where the owner has them and flag wall loss early enough for a spool to be ordered before the next docking.

faqs.q: What ship inspection in Le Havre can be combined with thickness gauging on the same visit?
faqs.a: Magnetic particle or penetrant crack detection at hatch corners, coaming brackets and other fatigue-prone details; UT of welds on recent repairs; and wall-thickness checks on ballast, fuel, sea-water or fire-main piping. On a short call it makes sense to combine them, because the team is already through the gate and the permits are in place.
